investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) — All Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval cannot provision a new agent, so no vmId or remoteState evidence is collected, causing the expected-output contract to go entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 agents per org (or globally, scope unclear from evidence). At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T23:02:34Z), that limit was already at or above 100, so POST /api/agents returned 409 with code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because agent creation is the prerequisite for every downstream remote-agent check, all three sibling checks fail with the identical error before any VM provisioning or state assertion can be evaluated.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} — observed in failedCheck.message

All three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure occurs at the creation step before any downstream assertion is reached
Expected-output contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready]; evidence object is empty ({}) for all three checks, meaning no agent was ever provisioned

Latency for all three failing calls is well under the warningLatencyMs threshold (1428ms, 1230ms, 988ms vs 30000ms warning), confirming the 409 is returned immediately by the quota guard — not a timeout or infrastructure slowness
The nested swarm error code is "conflict" with message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", indicating the swarm layer itself enforces the cap and surfaced it through the API layer
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval environment's org (or the shared swarm namespace used by the eval harness) has accumulated 100 live agents and none have been cleaned up — either prior eval runs leaked agents, or a cleanup/teardown step is missing or broken
[Likely] The eval harness creates a new agent on each run but does not delete it afterward, causing agents to accumulate across runs until the quota is hit
[Possible] A separate process, user, or automated job has provisioned agents against the same org/namespace up to the quota limit, leaving no room for the eval's agent
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a swarm configuration change, causing previously-passing evals to start failing without any change to the eval itself
[Less likely] The swarm backend has a bug where it counts deleted or terminated agents toward the quota, making the effective available slots lower than expected

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (HTTP 409) Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend rejected agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Since the eval harness cannot create a new agent, no agent ID, ready state, or runtime state can be collected, causing every downstream check to fail before producing any required evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100 for the target org/environment. At the time the eval ran (2026-06-14T23:02:36–38Z), that quota was already exhausted, so POST /api/agents returned 409 Conflict with the nested error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because all three checks share the same agent-creation step as their entry point, the quota breach caused a total eval failure for the entire remote-agents feature. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence of user-traffic impact or a broader service outage is present in the supplied data.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned the identical 409 error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}

The outer error message 'swarm agent already exists' combined with the inner 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' indicates the swarm layer is at its maximum agent count and is rejecting new creation requests.

Latencies for all three failing calls (1230 ms, 1428 ms, 988 ms) are well below the configured warningLatencyMs (5000 ms) and outageLatencyMs (20000 ms), confirming the failures are quota-driven rejections, not timeouts or infrastructure slowness.
The expectedOutputContract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, and state — none of these could be collected because agent creation was blocked before any agent was provisioned.
No evidence object was populated in any of the three checks, consistent with the eval aborting at the creation step with no agent to poll.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval org/account used in the production eval environment has accumulated 100 swarm agents (the hard limit) from prior eval runs that were not cleaned up, exhausting the quota.
[Likely] The eval teardown/cleanup step that should delete the test agent after each run is failing silently or not executing, causing agents to accumulate across runs until the quota is hit.

[Possible] The quota limit of 100 is shared between eval/test agents and real user agents in the same org, and legitimate user activity has consumed the quota, leaving none available for the eval harness.
[Less likely] The quota limit itself was recently lowered (e.g., from a higher value to 100) by a configuration or policy change, causing previously passing evals to suddenly fail.
[Less likely] A race condition or duplicate-creation bug in the eval harness is creating agents without deduplication, accelerating quota exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.details: Confirm whether the quota is fully consumed by listing existing agents for the org used by the eval harness.

reproductionSteps.details: Look for errors or skipped steps in the eval runner's agent-deletion phase to determine whether cleanup is executing successfully after each run.

reproductionSteps.details: After freeing quota by removing stale test agents, trigger the remote-agents eval suite again to confirm all three checks pass when quota is available.

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (409 Conflict) Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T23:02 with identical 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval cannot provision a new agent to complete its test lifecycle, so no expected-output contract evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is returning "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on POST /api/agents, meaning the org-level (or global) agent quota of 100 has been exhausted. Because the eval workflow depends on successfully creating a new agent as its first step, every downstream check (state, runtime) also fails — not due to independent faults, but because agent creation is a shared prerequisite. This is an eval-blocking infrastructure quota condition, not necessarily a user-facing outage, though real users attempting to create agents in the same quota scope would encounter the same 409.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three sibling checks: remote-agent-create (endedAt 23:02:36.301Z), remote-agent-state (endedAt 23:02:37.531Z), and remote-agent-runtime (endedAt 23:02:38.519Z).

All three error payloads are identical: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The nested swarm error explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the quota ceiling has been reached.
Latencies for all three calls were well under the warningLatencyMs threshold (988ms, 1428ms, 1230ms vs 20000ms warning / 60000ms outage), ruling out a timeout or performance degradation as the cause.
No expected-output contract evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message all absent), consistent with creation failing before any agent lifecycle data could be produced.
The check config marks this check as required: false, scoping the blast radius to eval observability rather than a hard production gate.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] A previous eval run (or runs) created agents and did not clean them up, causing leaked eval agents to accumulate against the quota until the limit of 100 was reached.
[Likely] The eval environment shares an agent quota with production or staging workloads, and organic user or system activity has consumed the quota independently of the eval.
[Possible] The eval teardown/cleanup step is missing, broken, or not being executed on failure paths, so each failed run leaves a stranded agent behind.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 is misconfigured or too low for the combined load of eval runs plus real workloads in this environment.
[Less likely] A separate process or automated job is creating agents in bulk against the same quota scope without a corresponding cleanup.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image generation stream eval failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame and never producing the required `generation_completed` frame or an artifact URL. The harness is either not deployed, misconfigured, or running an incompatible version at the target URL.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The stream received an HTTP 404 when attempting to open a session, which caused an immediate `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame. No progress frames, completion frames, or artifact URLs were ever emitted. This is an eval-environment infrastructure or configuration failure — there is no evidence of impact to production user traffic in the supplied signals.
proof: The `generation_error` frame carries code `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` and message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
The stream sequence is: generation_start → generation_error → empty message frame. No `generation_completed` frame was ever emitted.
Both required evidence fields (`frameTypes`, `imageUrlPresent`) are reported as missing in the check failure message.
The assertion `frameTypes contains generation_completed` cannot be satisfied because the stream terminated at the error frame.
The assertion `imageUrlPresent equals true` cannot be satisfied because no artifact was produced.
Total latency was 2085 ms — well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms — confirming the stream failed fast on a connection/routing error, not a timeout.
possibleCauses: (Most likely) The agent runtime harness is not deployed or not running at the URL referenced by LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL in the eval environment, causing every session-open request to return 404.
(Likely) The harness IS deployed but the configured base URL is wrong — e.g., a stale, incorrect, or environment-specific URL was used, pointing to a route that no longer exists or was renamed.
(Possible) The harness is running an incompatible version whose session-open endpoint path has changed, making the 404 a route-mismatch rather than a missing service.
(Less likely) A proxy, ingress, or service-mesh rule is intercepting the request and returning 404 before it reaches the harness process.
(Less likely) The harness deployment was recently torn down or scaled to zero replicas in the eval environment and was not restarted before the eval run.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image generation stream eval failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame and never producing the required `generation_completed` frame or an artifact URL. The harness is either not deployed, misconfigured, or running an incompatible version at the target URL.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The stream received an HTTP 404 when attempting to open a session, which caused an immediate `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame. No progress frames, completion frames, or artifact URLs were ever emitted. This is an eval-environment infrastructure or configuration failure — there is no evidence of impact to production user traffic in the supplied signals.
proof: The `generation_error` frame carries code `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` and message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
The stream sequence is: generation_start → generation_error → empty message frame. No `generation_completed` frame was ever emitted.
Both required evidence fields (`frameTypes`, `imageUrlPresent`) are reported as missing in the check failure message.
The assertion `frameTypes contains generation_completed` cannot be satisfied because the stream terminated at the error frame.
The assertion `imageUrlPresent equals true` cannot be satisfied because no artifact was produced.
Total latency was 2085 ms — well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms — confirming the stream failed fast on a connection/routing error, not a timeout.
possibleCauses: (Most likely) The agent runtime harness is not deployed or not running at the URL referenced by LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL in the eval environment, causing every session-open request to return 404.
(Likely) The harness IS deployed but the configured base URL is wrong — e.g., a stale, incorrect, or environment-specific URL was used, pointing to a route that no longer exists or was renamed.
(Possible) The harness is running an incompatible version whose session-open endpoint path has changed, making the 404 a route-mismatch rather than a missing service.
(Less likely) A proxy, ingress, or service-mesh rule is intercepting the request and returning 404 before it reaches the harness process.
(Less likely) The harness deployment was recently torn down or scaled to zero replicas in the eval environment and was not restarted before the eval run.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) — All Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval cannot provision a new agent, so no vmId or remoteState evidence is collected, causing the expected-output contract to go entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 agents per org (or globally, scope unclear from evidence). At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T23:02:34Z), that limit was already at or above 100, so POST /api/agents returned 409 with code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because agent creation is the prerequisite for every downstream remote-agent check, all three sibling checks fail with the identical error before any VM provisioning or state assertion can be evaluated.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} — observed in failedCheck.message

All three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure occurs at the creation step before any downstream assertion is reached
Expected-output contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready]; evidence object is empty ({}) for all three checks, meaning no agent was ever provisioned

Latency for all three failing calls is well under the warningLatencyMs threshold (1428ms, 1230ms, 988ms vs 30000ms warning), confirming the 409 is returned immediately by the quota guard — not a timeout or infrastructure slowness
The nested swarm error code is "conflict" with message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", indicating the swarm layer itself enforces the cap and surfaced it through the API layer
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval environment's org (or the shared swarm namespace used by the eval harness) has accumulated 100 live agents and none have been cleaned up — either prior eval runs leaked agents, or a cleanup/teardown step is missing or broken
[Likely] The eval harness creates a new agent on each run but does not delete it afterward, causing agents to accumulate across runs until the quota is hit
[Possible] A separate process, user, or automated job has provisioned agents against the same org/namespace up to the quota limit, leaving no room for the eval's agent
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a swarm configuration change, causing previously-passing evals to start failing without any change to the eval itself
[Less likely] The swarm backend has a bug where it counts deleted or terminated agents toward the quota, making the effective available slots lower than expected

investigations.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (HTTP 409) Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend rejected agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Since the eval harness cannot create a new agent, no agent ID, ready state, or runtime state can be collected, causing every downstream check to fail before producing any required evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100 for the target org/environment. At the time the eval ran (2026-06-14T23:02:36–38Z), that quota was already exhausted, so POST /api/agents returned 409 Conflict with the nested error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because all three checks share the same agent-creation step as their entry point, the quota breach caused a total eval failure for the entire remote-agents feature. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence of user-traffic impact or a broader service outage is present in the supplied data.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned the identical 409 error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}

The outer error message 'swarm agent already exists' combined with the inner 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' indicates the swarm layer is at its maximum agent count and is rejecting new creation requests.

Latencies for all three failing calls (1230 ms, 1428 ms, 988 ms) are well below the configured warningLatencyMs (5000 ms) and outageLatencyMs (20000 ms), confirming the failures are quota-driven rejections, not timeouts or infrastructure slowness.
The expectedOutputContract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, and state — none of these could be collected because agent creation was blocked before any agent was provisioned.
No evidence object was populated in any of the three checks, consistent with the eval aborting at the creation step with no agent to poll.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval org/account used in the production eval environment has accumulated 100 swarm agents (the hard limit) from prior eval runs that were not cleaned up, exhausting the quota.
[Likely] The eval teardown/cleanup step that should delete the test agent after each run is failing silently or not executing, causing agents to accumulate across runs until the quota is hit.

[Possible] The quota limit of 100 is shared between eval/test agents and real user agents in the same org, and legitimate user activity has consumed the quota, leaving none available for the eval harness.
[Less likely] The quota limit itself was recently lowered (e.g., from a higher value to 100) by a configuration or policy change, causing previously passing evals to suddenly fail.
[Less likely] A race condition or duplicate-creation bug in the eval harness is creating agents without deduplication, accelerating quota exhaustion.
